main_text.p: Perspicu-itaspuritate conjunctam vifus noftri aciem fugit: tum permeabilitas, qua fe in meatus corporum infinuat, poros permeat, & fe ipfo implet.
Perspicuitas aeris eft, qua radiis & lumini tenuis ejus substantia eft pervia.
MobilitasMobilitas aeris eft, qua multis & magnis permutationibus, & commotionibus, variisque impressionibus agitari & turbari aptus eft.

Aeris af-fectiones externa.Externae affectiones extrinsecus & mutabiliter accidunt: funtq; trium fere generum. 1. Aer jam calidus, jam frigidus eft, quippe fua natura utriusq; qualitatis capax ab interno principio aut incalescens aut frigescens. 2. Aer eft humidus, vel siccus. Humidus, cum ipse in se liquidus & fluidus imbibit aqueam humiditatem, vel pluviosam, vel vaporosam. Siccus eft aer, cum a radiis & calore Solis, vel a quorundam ventorum perseverantia siccatur. 3. Aer aut eft luminosus, aut tenebricosus. Luminosus, cum aer per se pellucidus recepto lumine illustratur; Tenebricosus, cum absente lumine obscuratur.

page.notes: The signature mark at the bottom left is faint; read as "H" with uncertainty. The running head letters are widely spaced in print and are given as LIBRI SECVNDI. Marginal notes were read from the left margin, which is the only margin with text. Long s rendered as s throughout. The word "meatus" is hyphenated at the line end as "mea-tus" and is written whole.
